'''''Aizoon canariense''''' is a species of small leafy [[annual plant]] in the family [[Aizoaceae]].<ref name="Tropicos">{{cite web|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/700374|title=Aizoon canariense|publisher=Tropicos|accessdate=28 November 2018}}</ref> 

==Description==
The plant can grow up to {{Convert|25|cm|frac=2}} tall. Its branches spread on the ground, its leaves are [[Petiole (botany)|petiolate]], somewhat fleshy and hairy. It has small flowers with {{Convert|1–3|mm|frac=16}} long sepals, yellowish inside, and no petals.<ref name=floracan>[http://www.floradecanarias.com/aizoon_canariense.html Aizoon canariense] at Flora de Canarias</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The plant can be found in warm arid to semi-arid areas including [[Macaronesia]] (on [[Madeira]], [[Canary Islands]] and [[Cape Verde]]), [[Arabia]], [[Pakistan]], [[North Africa]] and [[Southern Africa]].<ref>[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:360472-1 Aizoon canariense], [[Plants of the World Online]]</ref>

== Uses ==
[[Bedouin]]s of Egypt made a [[gruel]] from the ground seeds<ref>{{cite journal |last=Osborn |first=Dale J. |date=1968 |title=Notes on the Medicinal and Other Uses of Plants in Egypt |journal=Economic Botany |language=en |publisher=Springer on behalf of New York Botanical Garden Press |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=175 |doi=10.1007/BF02860560 |jstor=4252946 |s2cid=26895152}}</ref> and the leaves are locally [[Famine food|consumed in times of famine]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fern |first=Ken |date=2024-10-13 |title=Aizoon canariense |url=https://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Aizoon+canariense#:~:text=The%20plant%20is%20sometimes%20gathered,for%20local%20use%20as%20food. |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Useful Tropical Plants Database}}</ref>
